item.title: Strike on Ukrainian public bus leaves 30 dead as blackouts worsen in Kyiv
item.description: Russian strikes in eastern Ukraine have killed 30 people and injured at least 18, according to authorities. The attacks included a strike on a public bus and have worsened power outages in Kyiv.

item.title: ICE has quietly used this warehouse as a detention facility all summer, neighbors say
item.description: Throughout the summer, rumors have been bubbling in North New Jersey that ICE has quietly been using a warehouse as a detention center. NPR investigated.

item.title: Medical debt is crushing hospital patients in LA. Health officials may have a fix
item.description: In Los Angeles County, the nation's most populous, a new system could screen hospital patients for financial aid, preventing hundreds of thousands from getting bills they can't pay.

item.title: As crypto and prediction markets expand, their regulator shrinks

item.title: Syrian general accused of atrocities is protected by U.S. and Lebanon, NPR and BBC find

item.title: Toss-ups, triage and targets: How to read the wide-open 2026 House map
item.description: Both parties are spending heavily in roughly 60 House districts — where Trump won by an average of nine points in 2024 — that could be key to deciding control of the chamber, an NPR analysis finds.

item.title: Maricarmen, the 87-year-old woman whose eviction shook Spain, has died
item.description: María del Carmen Abascal, the 87-year-old woman whose eviction from her Madrid home sparked nationwide protests across Spain and unleashed a political crisis, died on Wednesday while hospitalized.
